newsitem.title: USA: Plains cattle trade nil after active Tuesday - trade.
newsitem.headline: Plains cattle trade nil after active Tuesday - trade.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets early Wednesday were quiet following Tuesday's active trading, feedlot sources said.

Cattle Tuesday sold at a top of $72.00 per cwt in the southern/central Plains, steady with last week. An estimated 41,000 head sold in Kansas and about 30,000 in the Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma, cattle feeders said. Totals were expected to climb as final tallies were recorded, they said.
Many of the cattle sold were slated for normal seven-day pickup, although a few loads in Kansas had an extra day tacked on, sources there said.
Feedlot cattle prices were underpinned by tight supplies of finished cattle that would grade choice and by continued firm beef demand, market sources said.
Beef prices Tuesday were quoted up $1.46 to $1.69 per cwt for choice supplies and up $0.12 to down $0.42 for select, on 253 loads of fabricated cuts sold, according to USDA.
The choice lighter-weight beef price was up $1.69 at $117.60, the highest level in over three years, since August 19, 1993.
